lines.text: Mortgage rates finally dropped. Here's why it barely helps.
lines.say: Mortgage rates finally dropped. Here's why it barely helps.

lines.text: On Thursday, Freddie Mac said the average 30-year rate fell to 7.32%.
lines.say: On Thursday, Freddie Mac said the average thirty-year rate fell to seven point three two percent.

lines.text: That's down from 7.40%, the first weekly drop since August.
lines.say: That's down from seven point four percent, the first weekly drop since August.

lines.text: A year ago, that same average was just 6.19%.
lines.say: A year ago, that same average was just six point one nine percent.

lines.text: Example: on a $400,000 loan, principal and interest goes from about $2,447 a month to $2,748.
lines.say: Take a four hundred thousand dollar example loan. Principal and interest goes from about two thousand four hundred forty-seven a month to two thousand seven hundred forty-eight.

lines.text: That's about $300 more every month, or roughly $3,600 a year.
lines.say: That's about three hundred dollars more every month, or roughly thirty-six hundred dollars a year.

lines.text: Thursday's dip saves that same borrower only about $22 a month.
lines.say: Thursday's dip saves that same borrower only about twenty-two dollars a month.

lines.text: That average also assumes great credit and 20% down. Real quotes vary.
lines.say: That average also assumes great credit and twenty percent down. Real quotes vary.

lines.text: One week isn't a trend. The next Freddie Mac reading comes October 29.
lines.say: One week isn't a trend. The next Freddie Mac reading comes October twenty-ninth.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Mortgage rates finally fell. Here's why it barely helps
post.ig:
Mortgage rates finally fell. Here's why it barely helps.
Freddie Mac: the average 30-year fixed rate was 7.32% on Oct 22, 2026, down from 7.40%, the first weekly drop since August.
A year ago it was 6.19%.
Example: on a $400,000 loan, principal and interest is about $2,748 a month at 7.32% vs. $2,447 at 6.19%, about $300 more.
The latest dip saves that borrower about $22 a month.
Sources: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (Oct 22, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
